newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds-Southern mills brace for storm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds-Southern mills brace for storm.

text.p: Many feed mills in North Carolina may be shutting down early, as they prepare for Hurricane Fran's arrival late on Thursday or early Friday, U.S. brokers and millfeed sources said.
In North Carolina, Gov. James Hunt declared a state of emergency for all of the state's 100 counties.

"People are trying to button up," one Carolina broker said. "Flour mills (in the Carolinas) have sold their spot and there is not anything extra," he said. "The storm is coming in and the feed mills from Sanford, N.C. on east will be shutting down."

"This is true," another North Carolina millfeed source said. "By 5:00 or 6:00 (pm EDT), all the feed mills along the eastern North Carolina coast will probably shut down on a temporary basis, he said. He noted that usually the feed mills run from 5-1/2 to 6-1/2 days on a 24-hour basis.
In the North Carolina's Rosehill area where several feedmills are clustered, preparations are already being made.
"We are making plans because we will not have any power early this evening," one Rosehill mill source said, who declined to be identified.
Some sources said mills may be back up early Friday if they have power.
Elsewhere, the St Louis market was seen very solid for next week. One dealer noted that demand was outpacing supply.
"Things are tightening in St Louis and it is not because of the holidays. We are getting buyers from Missouri and Arkansas."
